name: Turks and Caicos Islands

findings.local_actor: LIME Turks and Caicos (Cable & Wireless, now Flow)
findings.summary: LIME (Cable & Wireless) launched 4G LTE in the Turks and Caicos Islands, covering Providenciales, Grand Turk and South Caicos, with Ericsson deploying the network under the operator's Project Marlin capital programme.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) treated as controller under the equipment-vendor rule, pole third. The US$1.05bn Project Marlin figure is region-wide, not TCI-specific, so no value is recorded. Whether Ericsson still supplies Flow TCI's current RAN/core (including any later 5G or vendor swap) was not confirmed, so still_current null; TeleSemana likely relays the operator release.

findings.summary: Digicel, licensed in Turks and Caicos in spring 2006, built and launched its GSM network there with equipment from Ericsson, then described as Digicel Group's exclusive infrastructure provider across its Caribbean markets.
findings.analyst_inference: Both sources are from one publisher, so not independent corroboration. This is a 2006 GSM build; Digicel's current TCI LTE/core vendor was not found, so the Ericsson relationship may not describe today's network. still_current null; pre-2020 finding.

findings.controller: Digicel Turks and Caicos (Digicel Group), installer and maintainer
findings.local_actor: Royal Turks and Caicos Islands Police Force / Turks and Caicos Islands Government (911 Centre)
findings.summary: Police reported a public CCTV network of over 100 HD cameras on Providenciales feeding a new 911 control room, with Digicel contracted to install and maintain cameras, video-management software, servers and storage; FortisTCI hosts cameras on its poles.

sources.publisher: Royal Turks and Caicos Islands Police Force

findings.analyst_inference: Camera and VMS manufacturer not named in either source; Digicel is documented as maintaining the system, so it is treated as controller (Caribbean group, pole third). If the cameras or VMS turn out to be Hikvision/Dahua, pole would change. Police said about US$800,000 had been spent on CCTV and 911 infrastructure combined; that is spend-to-date, not a contract value, so not recorded. FortisTCI release cited as S4 (corporate). Phase-two expansion to Grand Turk was planned; current status unconfirmed.

findings.local_actor: Turks and Caicos Islands Government / TCI Telecommunications Commission
findings.summary: The government, via the Telecommunications Commission, commissioned Cambridge Management Consulting to prepare an outline business case for a domestic inter-island submarine fibre system, replacing outage-prone microwave links; TCI's international connectivity relies on ARCOS-1.
findings.analyst_inference: Planning stage only (consultancy, tier 2); no cable supplier, builder or financier named, so pole null: the controller under the equipment-vendor rule is not yet determined. DCD reports a January 2023 consultant tender for a national fibre ring linked to ARCOS-1; treated as the same domestic-connectivity initiative, which a reviewer should confirm. Cambridge MC page is the consultant's own marketing (S4).
